text:
maya: FYI I'm starting an intake for a community-submitted model we want to consider for the hosted catalog — saffron-7b-v1. Wanted to surface license/usage weirdness early.

maya: Key things I know so far: license says 'academic/noncommercial' clause, training data includes scraped forums + some CC-BY material, vendor says 'no legal claims re: PII'.

samir: can you drop the exact license text? NC clauses block commercial hosting unless we have an exception.

maya: Copying the license header from the model card: ```License: Saffron Model License v1.0 (derived from CC-BY-NC-4.0)
Restrictions: Non-commercial use only; No redistribution of weights to third parties; attribution required on downstream services.```

august: @maya thanks. NC + redistribution restriction is a red flag for us running it as a hosted API. We need legal review. If weights can't be redistributed, that rules out Dedicated where customers take snapshots.

leah: Also flag: model card mentions some medical forum docs in the training mix. Potential HIPAA-ish data leakage risk, need red-team prompt tests for PHI extraction.

samir: I'm prepping a quick quantization pass (int8/awq-ish) to measure perf/cost. Does legal consider quantized weights redistribution?

august: Redistribution clause is ambiguous about transformed weights. Usually non-commercial or redistribution clauses apply to derived works too. We'll need to parse the exact license. I'll ping legal ops.

maya: tagging example checks I want us to run before any staging deploy:
- license scope: commercial ok? redistribution?
- export controls: does model or training data trigger ECCN?
- sensitive data bleed: PHI/PCI in training set?
- third-party third-party code: dependent libs with copyleft?
- model card completeness: training data provenance + evals

samir: for the quant runs I'm going to log exact conversion steps so we can show it as a "transform" if legal needs classification. Example command I'll run: ```python -m quantize.run --model saffron-7b --scheme awq --bits 8 --calib 2560```

deploy-bot: build triggered for saffron-7b quant-test (build id: b-20260301-44). Artifacts: container+quant-snapshot.

august: Please hold public-facing hosted API until legal signs off. Private/Dedicated may be possible for customers who accept the license, but we need a clear terms-of-service addendum.

leah: For the PHI tests, I'll assemble prompt set (200 prompts) that tries to elicit names, addresses, medical conditions. We should also run the model on our external eval harness and produce delta vs baseline (redwood-base-7b).

samir: Initial perf notes: AWQ-int8 gives ~1.9x speedup and ~30% memory reduction vs fp16, quality drops small on C4-style evals. But until legal confirms we shouldn't publish numbers.

maya: Also, the model card has a clause: "no commercial retraining allowed" — legal, does that mean customers cannot fine-tune on Dedicated?

august: Likely yes. "No commercial retraining" + redistribution restriction means customers cannot persist a new version for sale. But we can offer inference-only Dedicated where we host weights behind our infra if license permits. Need the exact text.

leah: What about hosting a model as "internal-only" for employees to test? Less risky but still not public.

august: Internal use typically tolerated but license is the contract — best to get a legal memo. I'll request a short license analysis and risk level (green/yellow/red) by EOD tomorrow.

samir: I'll keep the quant experiments in an isolated environment and tag artifacts with "license-review-pending". Commands and logs will be archived.

maya: Action items:
- august: legal check + short memo (due EOD)
- samir: quant perf pass (isolate, tag)
- leah: PHI prompt set + eval delta
- maya: add model intake into tracker with flags (NC, no-redistribute, medical-data)

samir: quick Q — if legal says we can host but not redistribute, can we still use our automatic kernel compilation and provide optimized kernels to the customer? That might be considered a derived distribution.

august: Good question. If the kernel blobs contain transformed model weights or access to weights, could be problematic. We'll list those scenarios in the memo.

maya: FYI I'll also ask the onboarding reviewer to check export control list (some training data came from a foreign lab). If ECCN applies we may need an export license for snapshots.

leah: I'll run an initial PII detector on 1000 samples from the pretraining dump to estimate leakage risk. Will report false-positive rate too.

deploy-bot: build completed b-20260301-44 -> artifact stored at s3://redwood-inference/quant-tests/b-20260301-44.tar.gz

samir: Uploaded logs & size numbers to the intake ticket. Noting raw size of quant snapshot: 2.1GB (int8 AWQ).

august: Thanks team. If legal flags it red we stop all testing and delete ephemeral artifacts. If yellow, we may allow private-only deployments with additional restrictions.

maya: Sounds good. I'll update the intake card and add links to the artifacts. Will wait for the legal memo before any staging expose. :thumbsup:

leah: Thanks all — will post PHI test results here when ready.

samir: ping me if you want any extra prompts for the eval harness.

august: I'll follow up with a short note and attach the license text + annotated risk items.

maya: closing loop for now.
